nodes.label: rateLimit
nodes.rationale: A per-key fixed-window limiter returned as a handler wrapper; excess requests get 429 with Retry-After, and X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining let clients back off without retrying randomly. The key must be a value the client cannot forge - keying on x-forwarded-for lets an attacker rotate it per request and bypass the limit.

nodes.label: Fixed-window counting
nodes.rationale: Implemented with the cache's incr plus TTL, which is atomic across pods when backed by Redis. With InMemoryCache each pod keeps its own counter, so a client spread over 4 pods gets effectively 4x the limit - acceptable for permissive limits, problematic for strict ones.

nodes.label: Fixed-window edge effects
nodes.rationale: Bursts crossing a window boundary can deliver 2x the limit in seconds (100 at t=59s, 100 more at t=61s). The framework ships no sliding-window or token-bucket variant, so strict-burst protection must be implemented manually.

nodes.label: Dedicated cache instance for the limiter
nodes.rationale: The counter enforcing the limit is an ordinary cache entry and InMemoryCache evicts the least-recently-used one without knowing which entries carry security state. Share the instance with cached or idempotent and a caller minting distinct keys through either evicts other clients' counters, handing each a fresh budget - while the flooder's own counter is safe, because incr marks it most-recently-used on every request.
